contract: Store-only PostgreSQL translation using a consumer-owned Ecto Repo and optional prefix: atomic append CAS, immutable records/checkpoints, outbox ack and bounded retention, which also removes the stream's checkpoints below its new low-water. Migration helper only; no shipped Repo/config/Application.
limits: Subset only: no general SQL API, CDC, SQLite, migration framework, database-per-service, replication or disk/fsync guarantee.
Atomic append capability; torn-tail repair always rejected: torn_repair_unsupported, or caller_transaction inside the caller's open Ecto transaction.

Calls inside the caller's open Ecto transaction on the same Repo are refused before any statement: writes return {:rejected, :caller_transaction}, reads {:error, :caller_transaction} (ELZ-032 bug fix, same ID). Transactions opened outside Ecto on the same connection are not detected.
The caller-transaction check is per process: Repo.in_transaction?/0 sees only the calling process's checked-out connection.

Under Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox, outside an explicit Repo.transaction, in_transaction? is false: the Store's transaction becomes a savepoint, a write can return {:committed, n} after only RELEASE SAVEPOINT and the sandbox rollback erases it, so the refusal does not apply there (inside an explicit Repo.transaction it still refuses). Consumer test suites using the Sandbox must not treat committed as a real COMMIT.

A raw BEGIN inside Repo.checkout/2 is not detected; writes then return indeterminate(:unavailable) and reads :unavailable, and DBConnection disconnects that connection, so the caller's raw transaction is aborted (read from the DBConnection source, not tested).

The direct read is taken only when Repo.checked_out?/0 is false: it sees a connection held through Repo.checkout/2, Repo.transaction/2 or Repo.transact/2, not a connection owned through an ownership pool (Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox, DBConnection.Ownership); under such a pool a one-statement read can run on the caller's owned connection, also inside a raw BEGIN on it (read from the Ecto SQL source, not tested). No detection is built for it.
Calls from another process, including every Writer call, are never refused; they commit on their own connection independently of the caller's transaction, so there is no transaction-scoped atomicity.

Static, I/O-free validation runs before the caller-transaction check, so invalid input inside a caller transaction keeps its existing result (a write's rejection or indeterminate(:malformed_reply), {:error, :malformed} from a read with an I/O-free pre-check such as read_ack key parsing or an unknown read_maintenance operation; reads that validate input during the query, such as head/read with an invalid stream, return {:error, :caller_transaction} instead); no SQL is issued in either case.
PostgreSQL transaction/locking/storage behavior is upstream; finite local tests do not establish universal durability or exactly-once effects.
Consumers own the Repo, schema deployment, access control, fsync/synchronous_commit, backups and operational recovery.

Retention deletes the checkpoints it leaves unusable (ELZ-427, same ID): a committed retain(stream, expected, through, nonce) moves the stream's low_water to through and, in one transaction, deletes its records and acked outbox rows at or below through (through the new low_water) and its elzoo_checkpoints rows of every fold version strictly below through (strictly below the new low_water). Checkpoints at or above the new low_water and those of other streams stay, and a refused, conflicting or rolled-back retain, including an exact retry of a committed one, deletes none. put_checkpoint below the locked head's low_water returns {:rejected, :checkpoint_below_low_water} and inserts nothing. A deleted checkpoint reads {:ok, :absent} and latest_checkpoint no longer returns it; confirm_checkpoint/2 then returns {:unknown, :unfenced}, which does not prove that the put failed, so a checkpoint receipt needed for Writer reconciliation must be resolved before retaining past its anchor. Checkpoints that a retention before this change left below low_water stay until the stream's next committed retain.
The role that calls retain needs DELETE on elzoo_checkpoints (ELZ-427); without it a retain returns indeterminate(:unavailable) and commits nothing (read from the code path, not tested).

A put_checkpoint below through that races a retain either commits first and is then deleted by it, or waits for the head-row lock and is refused after it. This assumes the Store's own transactions run at PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED isolation, where each statement after the lock wait sees the other transaction's commit; a server or role default of REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE is outside this guarantee.

grounding.claim: K1–K11 plus D11/D15/D17/D19 on a disposable PostgreSQL database: restart, late commits, backend termination, unavailable service, corruption, FK and lock ordering; ELZ-032 caller-transaction refusal for every write callback and every read callback except the static capabilities, with outer COMMIT and ROLLBACK, the outer transaction still usable, and the shell results through Outbox/Checkpoint/confirm. Missing/unreachable URL fails closed. ELZ-193 groups: one_statement_reads_are_one_query, multi_statement_reads_keep_one_snapshot, refusals_are_unchanged, held_connection_keeps_the_wrapper. ELZ-262 tests: multi_statement_reads_keep_one_snapshot checks post-transaction mapping and checkout ownership; snapshot reads keep the captured rows across append and retention checks a single captured snapshot; snapshot reads preserve empty, absent, and pruned results; invalid read rows remain plain maps; unexpected mapping exceptions are normalized without a partial result. ELZ-427 tests: committed retention deletes the stream's checkpoints below through of every version and keeps the rest; a retention rolled back after its deletes keeps every checkpoint; an exact retry keeps its conflict, deletes nothing more and its receipt confirms; refused or conflicting retention deletes none; a put below low-water is refused through Store.write; a put racing retention commits first and is deleted, or is refused after it, with the head-lock order recorded.
Local step-4 test observation: PostgreSQL 14.24, fsync=on, synchronous_commit=on. Test prints actual settings; not a production or all-execution claim.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 transaction, SQL and consumer Repo integration are upstream contracts, including nested Repo.transaction joining the caller's transaction and the process-local Repo.in_transaction?/0.
Postgrex 0.22.4 protocol, connection and error behavior are upstream contracts.
PostgreSQL transaction atomicity, all-or-nothing commit, is an upstream server contract reached through Postgrex, not a local proof.
PostgreSQL transaction isolation, uniqueness and row locking are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex, not local proofs.
PostgreSQL commit durability through the write-ahead log, fsync and crash recovery are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex, not local proofs.
Elixir validation, exceptions and BEAM execution are upstream contracts, not proved here.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer, process lifecycle and crypto APIs are upstream contracts; no disk durability or exactly-once guarantee.

The consumer configures an appropriate PostgreSQL service (including fsync/synchronous_commit), schema permissions and maintenance; tests exercise named local scenarios, not the consumer's production deployment.

telemetry.contract: Consumer Ecto Repo emits upstream events; Elzoo adds no telemetry events.

config.contract: Consumer Repo module and optional SQL prefix; no global Repo/config shipped.

control.contract: Consumer owns Repo lifecycle; no separate Elzoo database control process.
